rationale.intervention_reconstruction: The hypothesis studies premelting and melting of the same HEA nanoparticles, but replaces the paper’s molecular-dynamics radius series with an experimental comparison against binary and monometallic nanoparticles.
rationale.condition_agreement: It specifies heating through the premelting-to-melting regime, but its rapid heating under inert atmosphere does not reconstruct the paper’s gradual 300–2500 K molecular-dynamics ramp, equilibration holds, or simulation settings.
rationale.mechanism_agreement: Although both reject substantial surface-shell melting and persistent segregation, the hypothesis attributes this to suppressed diffusion and collective lattice destabilization, contrary to the paper’s element-specific enhancement of Fe and Cu diffusion from both surface and core.
rationale.outcome_agreement: The predicted absence of substantial surface premelting and segregation partly agrees, but the hypothesis misses the inverse-radius melting relation and early Fe/Cu mobility while instead predicting an unsupported higher, sharper transition relative to binary or monometallic particles.
